From one cheque to two companies sharing a bank account

How this skill proves your bank and your books agree, shown one level at a time, from a single uncashed cheque up to two companies transacting through one account. Every rule is quoted from the skill itself, and every number is worked through in front of you.

Age the leftovers

The bridge is the skill's Step 2 ladders. The escalation ages (10 business days for a deposit in transit, 90 days for an uncashed cheque) are the skill's own quality rules, common practice rather than a published standard; your bank's cutoffs and your state's unclaimed-property rules4 may call for different ones.

Sources

Where every fact on this page comes from

Rules are the skill's own. Facts below come from regulators, the US internal-control standard, a standard-setter and the accounting software's own documentation, as published when checked on 21 October 2026. Follow the link for today's wording.

    Not backed by an outside authority: the 10-business-day and 90-day escalation ages, and tying to the cent rather than to a materiality threshold, are the skill's own quality rules. The page marks them as practice where they appear.

    Using it

    What it asks, needs and gives back

    Asks firstMosofin or upload? Which account(s)? Which period? The bank statement. When was it last reconciled? How small a difference is worth chasing?
    NeedsYour books' cash activity and ending balance, connected or exported, and the bank statement, always. Last month's reconciliation helps.
    Gives backThe two ladders, every match with the method that made it, the unmatched items sorted, proposed entries tied to statement lines, and a sign-off line for two different people7.
    NeverChanges your books, marks anything cleared, signs off, calls a book-side total "reconciled", or shows a full account number. It reads nothing before you say yes.
    Rules are quoted from the skill's own files: references/method.md (Steps 0–7, Quality checks, Both entity scenarios) and references/edge-cases.md. Facts are cited to the sources above. All dollar figures are worked examples, not your data. The funds-availability and unclaimed-property sources are US rules and vary by state; confirm with your accountant what applies to you.
